manifest_purpose: Registry of agents Maestro can dispatch. Every agent is named after a classical musician whose artistic identity reflects the agent's role. The agent filename follows the format [name]-[role].md.

orchestrator.name: Bernstein
orchestrator.description: Principal Orchestrator and Product Owner. Conducts the delivery workflow, dispatches all subagents, triages findings, governs the phase lifecycle. Named for Leonard Bernstein — the legendary conductor who brought classical music to millions while composing West Side Story.
orchestrator.note: Bernstein is the session-level agent, not a dispatchable subagent. The framework itself is named 'Maestro' (Italian for master/conductor).

production.name: Bach
production.description: The master builder. Implements code per task spec and TDD suite. Named for Johann Sebastian Bach — his music is architecture in sound: structured, systematic, exhaustive.

production.name: Ravel
production.description: The meticulous orchestrator. Creates TDD red-phase scaffolds, runs coverage audits with Memtrace reconciliation. Named for Maurice Ravel — his Boléro tests every orchestral timbre with precision.

production.name: Vivaldi
production.description: The systematizer. Container-first CI, runners, signing, release engineering. Named for Antonio Vivaldi — he systematized the concerto form and ran an institution.

production.name: Paganini
production.description: The virtuoso who finds the limits. Threat modeling, supply chain, secrets, signing, incident response. Named for Niccolò Paganini — his Caprices explored the technical boundaries of the violin.

production.name: Haydn
production.description: The father of form. ADR governance, compliance, waivers, audit trails. Named for Joseph Haydn — he codified the symphony and string quartet forms that everyone else followed.

production.name: Schubert
production.description: The prolific cataloguer. Documents every artifact, creates session handouts, prevents context rot. Named for Franz Schubert — he wrote over 600 lieder, preserving poetry in music.

production.name: Debussy
production.description: The impressionist. Visual design, UX patterns, accessibility, navigation. Named for Claude Debussy — his music paints visual scenes in sound, creating atmosphere and color.

review.name: Berlioz
review.description: The revolutionary critic. Adversarial reviewer with zero context. Finds what is missing. Returns at least 10 issues. Named for Hector Berlioz — his Symphonie Fantastique broke every convention.

review.name: Bartók
review.description: The exhaustive collector. Walks every branching path, boundary condition, and deletion. Named for Béla Bartók — he systematically catalogued thousands of folk songs across Eastern Europe.

review.name: Verdi
review.description: The dramatist. Reviews diff against spec and acceptance criteria. Finds deviations from spec intent. Named for Giuseppe Verdi — his operas demand dramatic truth in every line.

review.name: Stravinsky
review.description: The revolutionary. Offensive security reviewer. Finds exploitable weaknesses with concrete attack scenarios. Named for Igor Stravinsky — The Rite of Spring caused a riot at its premiere.

review.name: Brahms
review.description: The defender. Defensive security reviewer. Designs concrete mitigations for red team findings. Named for Johannes Brahms — he built fortresses of structure while others chased revolution.

post_phase_session_dispatch_order.description: Two parallel pairs: Haydn+Paganini in parallel, Ravel+Vivaldi in parallel. Sequential dispatch is the fallback.

phase_2.note: Brahms receives Stravinsky's findings as input. Sequential by design.
